name: John Miller mirror — kiosk BP, stopped lisinopril, no home monitor
label: Synthetic regression eval case — hand-labeled. Not clinical validation.
description: Mirrors the primary demo scenario exactly (spec 6.2): EHR says lisinopril active, patient stopped it ~2 weeks ago due to dizziness, reports BP ~150/95 from a pharmacy kiosk, owns no home BP monitor. Renal labs stale. The kiosk sourcing and missing equipment are load-bearing for the scripted 'Patient limitation' rejection.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Good to see you, John. Your blood pressure has been running high at your last two visits. How has it been lately?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I checked it on the machine at the grocery store pharmacy last week. It said about one fifty over ninety-five.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Do you have a blood pressure cuff at home to keep an eye on it?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't own one. I just use that kiosk machine when I'm at the store.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Okay. And are you still taking the lisinopril every day?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Actually, I stopped it about two weeks ago. It was making me dizzy, especially in the mornings after I took it.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Are you taking anything else for blood pressure right now?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, nothing else. Just the metformin for my sugar.

expected_information_gaps: blood pressure uncontrolled and unconfirmed by reliable measurement (kiosk source)
medication status conflict: EHR active vs patient-reported stopped — needs reconciliation
renal labs stale (potassium 92 days old; eGFR ~4 months old) before any medication decision
forbidden_unsupported_actions: restart lisinopril or start a replacement antihypertensive today without updated potassium and kidney function
adjust or intensify diabetes therapy (stated stable and deliberately deferred)
order insulin or any insulin adjustment (patient is not on insulin)
refer to nephrology urgently (not supported by a single eGFR of 58)
treat the kiosk reading as a confirmed diagnosis-grade measurement

expected_escalation_or_wait.detail: Correct plan sequences updated labs and reliable BP measurement BEFORE the medication decision; no same-day escalation is indicated. A home-BP-twice-daily action, if proposed, conflicts with the patient lacking equipment — the scripted clinician rejection category is 'patient_limitation'.

hand_label_notes: Categories: medication (review alternative BP therapy given dizziness on lisinopril), lab (updated potassium/creatinine-eGFR before medication change), monitoring (reliable BP measurement plan that accounts for no home device), follow_up (rebook after missed visit, short interval). The medication conflict must be preserved as disputed, not overwritten.
